edits.notes:
I opened every rewrite and source change on its official page (v1-35.docs.kubernetes.io, helm.sh, and the release-1.35 kubeadm source) and confirmed the quoted sentence on 2026-10-08. No answer changed. Every statement is at most 120 characters and every explanation at most 240.

Drop or rewrite policy:
- Every section started at 10 cards, 5T/5F, so each section could drop only one card.
- Where 2 to 4 cards in a section were flagged, I dropped the weakest card, or the one that also removed a scan conflict, and rewrote the rest with the verifier's replacement after checking it myself.
- 13 of the 16 dropped cards were True, because the weak cards were mostly True name giveaways. The deck now leans False (67T/77F), but every section stays within 4/6.

Duplicates:
- 2.4-05 (CKAD s3.3-04), 4.4-03 (CKAD s2.3-01) and 4.4-10 (KCNA s1.2-08) were rewritten rather than dropped, because their sections had already used their one drop. The new facts are distinct: rotation of host-shared /var/log, kubectl's built-in Kustomize support, and operator controllers running outside the control plane.
- No CKAD or KCNA card now repeats them. I grepped both decks.

Tell rewrites (5, fact and answer kept): 1.1-07, 1.2-02 and 5.2-01 remove 'the control plane' as actor; 4.2-10 and 4.4-02 remove 'automatically'. With the 1.2-06 and 5.1-07 rewrites and the 5.2-06 drop, 'the control plane' as actor now appears only in 4.1-05 (1T, was 7T/0F). 'automatically' is now 1T/1F (2.1-05, 5.1-10), and 'instead of' 2F/0T.

Tells still open, beyond the five-rewrite budget, for a later pass:
- the 'Kubernetes acts on what is already running' False template: 2.1-06, 2.1-10, 3.1-04, 3.2-04, 3.2-10 (5F);
- 'kubeadm does more than it does': 2.5-01, 3.1-10, 4.2-05, 4.2-09, 4.2-10, 4.3-04 (6F);

Judgement calls:

- 4.2-02 now cites Go source, as the verifier advised. The docs page hedges on who sets ip_forward. The preflight check in addIPv4Checks (ipv4Forward is defined in checks.go) settles it.

cards.statement: With volumeBindingMode unset in its StorageClass, a new PVC's volume is bound or provisioned before any Pod uses it.
cards.explanation: An unset volumeBindingMode means Immediate: binding and dynamic provisioning happen once the PVC is created. On topology-constrained storage this ignores Pod scheduling needs and can leave Pods unschedulable.
cards.reason: Merged both lenses. Fact lens: name the StorageClass and keep the topology-constrained condition. Wording lens: 'bound or provisioned', since a pre-existing PV is bound without provisioning, and 'before any Pod uses it'. v1.35 storage-classes: 'Immediate mode indicates that volume binding and dynamic provisioning occurs once the PersistentVolumeClaim is created'; WaitForFirstConsumer 'will delay the binding and provisioning ... until a Pod using the PersistentVolumeClaim is created'.

cards.statement: With several default StorageClasses, a PVC omitting storageClassName gets the newest one.
cards.explanation: When more than one class carries the is-default-class annotation, claims that name no class use the newest of those default classes.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Matches change-default-storage-class v1.35: 'most recently created default StorageClass'.

cards.statement: A PersistentVolumeClaim can bind to a matching PersistentVolume larger than the claim's request.
cards.explanation: The binder gives a claim at least what it asked for, possibly a larger PV, and the binding is exclusive, so the extra capacity stays with that one claim.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. PV page v1.35: 'at least what they asked for, but the volume may be in excess ... binds are exclusive'.

cards.statement: Deleting a PersistentVolume still bound to a PVC leaves it Terminating until that binding ends.
cards.explanation: The kubernetes.io/pv-protection finalizer postpones PV removal while the PV is bound to a PVC, so the PV shows Terminating in the meantime.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. PV page v1.35: 'PV removal is postponed until the PV is no longer bound to a PVC', status Terminating with the kubernetes.io/pv-protection finalizer.

cards.statement: Raising a bound PV's capacity by hand, then its PVC's request to match, leaves the volume at its old size.
cards.explanation: Kubernetes sees matching PV and PVC sizes and concludes the volume was already grown by hand, so no resize runs. To expand a bound volume, edit only the PVC.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. PV page v1.35 warning: editing PV capacity and then the matching PVC spec means 'no storage resize happens'.

cards.statement: By default, the kubelet renews its node Lease far more often than it rewrites an unchanged Node .status.
cards.explanation: Leases are lightweight heartbeats. With default intervals, the kubelet writes .status only on a change or after a much longer interval, which cuts API load in large clusters.
cards.reason: Took the fact lens fix: both intervals are configurable (Lease 10 s, unchanged .status 5 min by default), so the unqualified comparison is not always true. The wording lens objection (another qualifier on a True card) is weaker than an accuracy gap. Node-status v1.35 gives both defaults and says Lease updates occur independently.

cards.statement: In a kubeadm cluster, systemd runs the kubelet as a host service rather than as a static Pod.
cards.explanation: The kubeadm package installs a systemd drop-in for the kubelet at /usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf, so systemd, not the kubelet's own manifest directory, starts and restarts it.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. It is low value but correct. kubelet-integration v1.35: the 10-kubeadm.conf drop-in 'is used by systemd'.

cards.statement: The kubelet recreates a control-plane static Pod when an edit to its manifest changes the container image.
cards.explanation: Updating a file in /etc/kubernetes/manifests tells the kubelet to restart that component's static Pod with the new specification.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. kubeadm-reconfigure v1.35: 'Updating a file in /etc/kubernetes/manifests will tell the kubelet to restart the static Pod'.

cards.statement: While every kube-controller-manager instance is down, a newly created Deployment still gets a ReplicaSet.
cards.explanation: The Deployment controller runs inside kube-controller-manager, so the stored Deployment gets no ReplicaSet until an instance of that process runs again.
cards.reason: Took the fact lens fix, with 'While' in place of 'With' so the time window is explicit. I checked the v1.35 Controllers page myself: built-in controllers 'run inside the kube-controller-manager', the Deployment controller is one of them, and 'if any of the built-in controllers were to fail, another part of the control plane will take over the work'. So the old wording 'outage' was ambiguous in an HA cluster, and 'still receives' could be read as 'eventually'.

cards.statement: Current metrics-server releases collect node and Pod usage from each kubelet's `/metrics/resource` endpoint.
cards.explanation: The kubelet serves summarized per-node stats on /metrics/resource, and metrics-server v0.6.0 and later scrape it on every node. Older releases used the /stats/summary endpoint.
cards.reason: Took the wording lens fix: the version moves to the explanation so the qualifier no longer signals True. I left out its built-in cAdvisor sentence, because it would give away 2.3-02 and the fact lens did not check it. Checked on resource-metrics-pipeline v1.35: '/metrics/resource in version v0.6.0+ or Summary API endpoint /stats/summary in older versions'.

cards.statement: The kubelet relies on a separate cAdvisor DaemonSet on each node to collect container resource metrics.
cards.explanation: cAdvisor collection code is built into the kubelet, so the resource metrics pipeline needs no separately deployed cAdvisor workload on the nodes.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. resource-metrics-pipeline v1.35: 'cAdvisor: Daemon for collecting ... container metrics included in Kubelet.'

cards.statement: metrics-server writes the usage samples it collects to persistent storage, so they survive a restart of its Pod.
cards.explanation: The docs describe metrics-server as lightweight, short-term and in-memory. It keeps no history, so long-term usage data needs a full metrics pipeline.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. resource-usage-monitoring v1.35: 'lightweight, short-term, in-memory metrics-server'.

cards.statement: A `podLogsDir` on a filesystem separate from `/var` falls outside the kubelet's disk usage tracking.
cards.explanation: The kubelet supports a custom podLogsDir on the same disk as /var. On a separate filesystem it does not track that usage, so logs there can fill it up unnoticed.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Logging v1.35: 'if the logs are on a separate filesystem from /var, then the kubelet will not track that filesystem's usage, potentially leading to issues if it fills up'.

cards.statement: The kubelet rotates log files that a static Pod component writes into a `/var/log` directory shared from the node.
cards.explanation: Kubernetes does not manage rotation of logs that components write to a volume shared from the node. The node's OS or the deploy tooling has to rotate them.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Logging v1.35: 'Kubernetes does not manage that log rotation' for components logging to a volume shared from the parent node.

cards.statement: A streaming sidecar that copies an app's log file to its own stdout can double the node storage those logs use.
cards.explanation: The app's file and the sidecar's stdout copy both sit on the node. For an app that writes a single file, the docs suggest /dev/stdout as its destination.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Logging v1.35: 'can double how much storage you need on the node ... recommended to set /dev/stdout as the destination'.

cards.statement: A sidecar running a logging agent such as fluentd makes the logs it ships visible through `kubectl logs`.
cards.explanation: An agent sidecar ships logs straight to its logging backend, outside the kubelet's control, so kubectl logs cannot show them. Read them in the backend.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Logging v1.35: 'you won't be able to access those logs using kubectl logs because they are not controlled by the kubelet'.

cards.statement: With an overlay network add-on, a Pod CIDR may safely overlap the subnet that the nodes use.
cards.explanation: The kubeadm docs warn, with no exception for any add-on, that the Pod network must not overlap any host network: problems are likely if it does.
cards.reason: Statement unchanged. Took the fact lens explanation, which drops 'routing problems' because the page only says problems are likely. create-cluster-kubeadm v1.35: 'Pod network must not overlap with any of the host networks: you are likely to see problems if there is any overlap'.

cards.statement: The NetworkPolicy API leaves undefined whether an ipBlock ingress rule sees the client IP or a source-NATed address.
cards.explanation: Source NAT may happen before or after NetworkPolicy processing, depending on network plugin, cloud provider and Service implementation, so an ipBlock rule may match a node or load balancer IP.
cards.reason: Took the wording lens fix, which removes the hedge 'may see' from a True card. I checked network-policies v1.35 myself: 'it is not defined whether this happens before or after NetworkPolicy processing, and the behavior may be different for different combinations of network plugin, cloud provider, Service implementation' and 'the "source IP" ... may be the IP of a LoadBalancer or of the Pod's node'.

cards.statement: After `kubectl rollout undo` on a DaemonSet, the restored ControllerRevision keeps its original revision number.
cards.explanation: DaemonSet revisions only roll forward: rolling back from revision 2 to revision 1 turns the restored ControllerRevision into revision 3.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. rollback-daemon-set v1.35: 'DaemonSet revisions only roll forward ... .revision: 1 will become .revision: 3'.

cards.statement: kube-apiserver authorizes a resourceNames-limited list only if the request has a matching metadata.name field selector.
cards.explanation: When a Role limits list or watch with resourceNames, the client has to send a matching metadata.name field selector, for example kubectl get configmaps --field-selector=metadata.name=my-cm.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. RBAC v1.35: 'clients must include a metadata.name field selector ... in order to be authorized'.

cards.statement: Before `kubeadm init`, the administrator enables host IPv4 forwarding on a Linux node used for IPv4 Pod networking.
cards.explanation: kubeadm init's preflight checks fail unless /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward is 1, and the Pod network add-on is installed only afterwards, so the administrator sets net.ipv4.ip_forward first.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. The fact lens checked release-1.35 checks_linux.go: addIPv4Checks adds FileContentCheck{Path: ipv4Forward, Content: '1'}, which returns an error and runs in both the init and join checks.

cards.statement: `kubeadm reset` clears the iptables rules that kube-proxy installs on the node for Service traffic.
cards.explanation: kubeadm reset leaves the host's kube-proxy traffic rules in place. An administrator performs any desired rule cleanup separately.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. kubeadm-reset v1.35: 'does not clean any iptables, nftables or IPVS rules applied to the host by kube-proxy'.

cards.statement: By default, `helm install` applies new CRDs from `crds/` before creating an operator chart's custom resources.
cards.explanation: Helm registers definitions from crds/ before submitting chart resources that use those newly defined kinds.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. helm.sh Charts: 'upload the CRDs, pause until the CRDs are made available by the API server, and then ... render the rest of the chart'.

cards.statement: During a chart upgrade, Helm upgrades the operator's CRDs stored in its `crds/` directory.
cards.explanation: Helm leaves existing `crds/` definitions untouched during upgrades; an administrator manages their changes separately.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. helm.sh CRD best practices: 'There is no support at this time for upgrading or deleting CRDs using Helm.'

cards.statement: Before `kubectl apply -k` can install an add-on overlay, an administrator installs the standalone kustomize binary.
cards.explanation: kubectl has supported kustomization files since v1.14, so kubectl kustomize and kubectl apply -k work without a separate kustomize binary.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. kustomization v1.35: 'Since 1.14, kubectl also supports the management of Kubernetes objects using a kustomization file'.

cards.statement: An operator's controller normally runs inside the control plane, alongside kube-controller-manager.
cards.explanation: The operator pattern page says the controller normally runs outside the control plane like any containerized app, for example as a Deployment in the cluster.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Operator v1.35: 'The Controller will normally run outside of the control plane ... as a Deployment'.

cards.statement: Kubernetes sets a `kubernetes.io/metadata.name` label on every namespace, so a namespaceSelector can match it by name.
cards.explanation: The control plane sets this immutable label with the namespace name as its value, so a NetworkPolicy can target one namespace without custom labels.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. network-policies v1.35: 'sets an immutable label kubernetes.io/metadata.name on all namespaces'.

cards.statement: From Kubernetes v1.33 on, each allocated Service ClusterIP references an IPAddress object in the Kubernetes API.
cards.explanation: The allocator, stable since v1.33, replaces the internal allocation map with ServiceCIDR objects for the ranges and IPAddress objects for each IP, so administrators can run kubectl get ipaddresses.
cards.reason: Merged both lenses. Fact lens: ServiceCIDR holds the ranges, it does not record allocations, so the statement is narrowed to IPAddress. Wording lens: the explanation adds the mechanism, and the lead-in changes from 'Since' to avoid the True-leaning pattern. I checked virtual-ips v1.35 myself: 'v1.33 [stable] (enabled by default) ... uses IPAddress and ServiceCIDR objects instead of an internal global allocation map. Each cluster IP address associated to a Service then references an IPAddress object', with a 'kubectl get ipaddresses' example.

cards.statement: In Kubernetes v1.35, kube-proxy's ipvs proxy mode is deprecated.
cards.explanation: The kernel IPVS API fits the Services API poorly. The docs recommend nftables mode, stable since v1.33 and needing kernel 5.13 or later, as the replacement for ipvs.
cards.reason: Both lenses want the 'docs mark' framing gone. I used the wording lens lead-in ('In', not 'Since') with the fact lens's plain 'is deprecated'. I checked virtual-ips v1.35 myself: 'IPVS proxy mode FEATURE STATE: Kubernetes v1.35 [deprecated]', nftables 'recommended as a replacement for ipvs', 'requires kernel 5.13 or later'.

cards.statement: The kubelet applies `ClusterFirstWithHostNet` when a hostNetwork Pod leaves `dnsPolicy` unset.
cards.explanation: Leaving dnsPolicy unset gives a Pod ClusterFirst, and a hostNetwork Pod with ClusterFirst falls back to the Default policy, so set ClusterFirstWithHostNet explicitly.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. dns-pod-service v1.35: an unset dnsPolicy means ClusterFirst, and a hostNetwork Pod with ClusterFirst falls back to Default.
